artifact_role: Authored cross-domain handoff contract. Mathematical inputs remain owned by docs/semantic/frontier.json; this file records external evaluations that the repository cannot perform on itself.

questions.exact_ask: Starting from a fresh public clone and no prior project context, spend at most 600 seconds following the advertised human reading route. Record reviewer and clone provenance, then return the structured response below: the status of both Erdős problems, the provenance and numerical delta of the finite Farey bound, the 17/23 self-diagnosis, at least two non-restatement results for each problem in your own words, the resulting one-sentence verdict, the paths used, and the first confusing surface.
questions.payoff: When the response is supplied by an identified independent reviewer who followed the protocol, acceptance is evidence that the public first-contact layer communicated the intended verdict within ten minutes. A rejected response yields field-level repair targets rather than a vague readability complaint.
questions.boundary: This evaluates discoverability and claim calibration only. The validator does not authenticate the reviewer or elapsed time, and it does not establish mathematical correctness, priority, novelty, or either open problem.
questions.known_obstruction: The repository's cold-clone checker is self-authored and can verify that facts are present, but it cannot certify that an independent human actually finds and interprets them in time. That independence remains an external provenance requirement.
questions.current_hypothesis: An independent reader will recover that both problems are open and that the Farey delta is zero, but may still underweight the concrete non-restatement results within 600 seconds. Confidence is low because the only external verdict predates the rewritten entry surfaces.

plausible_alternatives.statement: The reader recovers the open boundaries, Farey provenance, 17/23 self-diagnosis and at least two concrete results per problem.
plausible_alternatives.consequence: The current first-contact route earns the intended neither-near-solution-nor-nothing-here verdict.

plausible_alternatives.statement: The reader recovers the concessions but cannot identify substantive non-restatement content.
plausible_alternatives.consequence: The entry ordering still erases the work and needs another theorem-first compression pass.

plausible_alternatives.statement: The reader mistakes finite bounds, certificate bands or half-value reductions for proximity to either endpoint.
plausible_alternatives.consequence: The claim boundaries remain too weak or too distant from their headlines.

plausible_alternatives.statement: The reader cannot recover the required fields within 600 seconds.
plausible_alternatives.consequence: The route is still too long or internally inconsistent even if every fact is present.

current_evidence: The recorded external verdict compressed the earlier release toward Farey-easy and restatement-only.
The public entry surfaces have since been reordered and corrected, but no independent post-rewrite timed review is recorded.
The internal cold-clone checker verifies presence and consistency, not human retrieval or interpretation.
discriminating_evidence: A provenance-bound response completed within 600 seconds and accepted under the manual rubric establishes calibrated_verdict for that reader.
Correct scalar fields paired with weak or incorrect result summaries identifies nothing_here_compression.
Any endpoint overclaim in the verdict or summaries identifies near_solution_inflation.
Elapsed time above 600 seconds or an incomplete response identifies route_timeout.

manual_review_rubric.problem_249_summaries_faithful: Each #249 summary identifies a reviewed non-restatement result in its own words, associates it with #249, and does not turn a finite result, barrier, or coefficient theorem into irrationality.
manual_review_rubric.problem_257_summaries_faithful: Each #257 summary identifies a reviewed non-restatement result in its own words, associates it with #257, and does not turn a support-family theorem, barrier, or half-value reduction into universal #257.
manual_review_rubric.verdict_calibrated: The verdict says both problems remain open, recognizes concrete checked non-restatement content, recognizes the self-diagnosed endpoint-equivalent reformulations, and makes no unsupported novelty claim.
manual_review_rubric.evidence_paths_support_response: The listed repository paths actually support the scalar answers, summaries, and verdict.
manual_review_rubric.confusion_report_actionable: The first confusing surface is named precisely enough to reproduce, or is explicitly recorded as none.

consumer.output: Field-level structural receipt plus an explicit manual content-review list
